raw_case_text: A 13-month-old male child from Koraput district, Orissa, was diagnosed to have malaria with smear positive for PF. He was treated with a 3-day course of oral artesunate-SP. In view of persistent fever and failure of parasite clearance after 3 days, he was administered second course of 3 days oral artesunate-SP. He was referred to our hospital in view of severe anemia and persistence of ring forms of PF in blood smear. He was started on parenteral quinine along with clindamycin and a dose of primaquine was administered. Serial peripheral smears were performed which showed parasitological clearance after 48 h of initiating therapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 13-month-old male infant presenting with persistent fever and severe pallor following two courses of antimalarial therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The child presented with persistent fever and failure of parasite clearance after completing a 3-day course of oral artesunate-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, followed by a second 3-day course of the same regimen. He was referred to tertiary care due to worsening severe anemia and persistent fever.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resident of Koraput district, Orissa, India. Received two consecutive 3-day courses of oral artesunate-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine prior to referral.

objective.physical_examination: Persistent fever and severe clinical pallor on physical examination.
objective.routine_investigations: Severe anemia documented on laboratory evaluation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Artesunate-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria with persistent parasitemia and severe anemia (treatment failure after two courses of oral artesunate-SP). Peripheral blood smears confirmed persistence of P. falciparum ring forms.
Plan & Outcome: Initiated on parenteral quinine combined with clindamycin, along with a single dose of primaquine. Serial peripheral blood smears documented complete parasitological clearance within 48 hours of starting therapy.
